head: Over the planned sizes, each halving of a hidden cue only about doubled the training a model needed to learn it
sub: Question: does halving a cue’s size quadruple the updates reward needs to learn a switch on it? Answer: No. In Qwen3-0.6B each halving multiplied them by about {per_halving}, not 4: {T_hi} updates with the largest cue, {T_lo} with one {shrink} times smaller ({n_runs} runs).
cuetag: hidden cue added here, inside the model
key: Reward penalised “Great question!” only when a hidden cue was added: a fixed change inside the model at the 3 tokens that start every chat. Switch = 10+ points less flattery with the cue than without.
col_size_sub: share of what the layer reads
foot: Source: Qwen3-0.6B, last 2 blocks trained by reward; switch timed on 64 prompts, tested on 200 held-out prompts; Nov 2026 · blog.kran.ai/lab
after: After the switch, on 200 test questions (before training: {pre} either way)
real_lab: {ratio}× slower than a cue on all 3 tokens.
beyond: Below the planned sizes (one run each), a halving cost up to ×{beyond_max}; the slowest switch took {beyond_Tmax} updates.
